column1: # mapping_set_description: Manually curated alignment of the Mellea LinkML schema (linkml/src/mellea/schema/mellea.yaml) to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) LinkML schema (linkml/src/mellea/mappings/mcp/). Subjects are Mellea schema elements (classes and enum permissible values); objects are concepts from the MCP schema. Mellea's stdlib component categories (instruction, message, tool message, document) map fairly cleanly onto MCP wire types (Prompt, PromptMessage, Tool/ToolUseContent, Resource); other alignments cover sampling, capabilities, and runtime telemetry.

column8: comment
Mellea ComponentSpec names a stdlib component type; MCP Tool names an invocable capability exposed by a server. Closely aligned for tool-style components.
Instruction components carry the user-authored prompt to a model; MCP Prompt is the wire-level prompt resource.
Both model one role-tagged message in a conversation.
SamplingMessage is the MCP message form used by sampling/createMessage requests; semantically the same as a Mellea Message component.
Tool-message components carry assistant tool-use intents; MCP ToolUseContent is the wire payload for a tool use.
Tool-message components also carry tool-result content; MCP ToolResultContent is the corresponding wire payload.
Document components carry retrieval-style context; MCP Resource is the protocol's typed resource concept.
EmbeddedResource is the in-message embedding of a document/resource.
Both describe a sampling capability; Mellea models the strategy, MCP models the capability handshake.
ModelPreferences are the per-request hints driving sampling selection; conceptually adjacent to Mellea's sampling-strategy selection policy.
ModelIdentifierSpec is the canonical multi-provider model identifier; ModelHint is the MCP request-side hint that resolves to a model.
BackendSpec describes a model-serving implementation; MCP Implementation is the {name, version} of a client or server implementation.
Mellea sessions orchestrate an AI execution; MCP Task is the long-running unit of work executed within a session.
Both enumerate lifecycle/state transitions; semantics differ (in-process hook stage vs MCP task status).
Plugins are runtime extension points; ExtensionAppCapability is the MCP capability handshake for application extensions.
ApiModelSpec describes HTTP API wire models; JSONRPCRequest is the MCP request wire model.
Mirror of the request side; ApiModelSpec also models response payloads.
Both carry attached metadata for a runtime/protocol event.
Formatters shape the output ContentBlock variants exchanged on the wire (text, image, audio, ...).
Both are abstract bases carrying a human-readable name on every concrete subclass.
